source_text: 4. Cod. f. 232 b. XLIV. 1. Πολλὰς πύλας διαγράφει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου Ἰεζεκιὴλ, καὶ περὶ ἑκάστης διηγήσατό τι· νῦν δὲ διηγεῖται τοῖς ἔχουσι ὦτα, περὶ τῆς πύλης τῶν ἁγίων τῆς βλεπούσης κατὰ ἀνατολάς· περὶ ἧς γέγραπται ὅτι ἡ πύλη αὕτη κεκλεισμένη ἔσται, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. —Οὐ μόνον ὅτι Κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοὺ Ἰσραὴλ διέρχεται διὰ τῆς πύλης, κέκλεισται, ἀλλʼ ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἡγούμενος κάθηται ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ πύλῃ τοῦ φαγεῖν ἔναντι Κυρίου κατὰ τὴν ὀδὸν Αἱλὰμ, ὅπερ ἐρ μηνεύεται πρόθυρον πύλης. —Πύλη ἐστὶ κεκλεισμένι, τὰ μυστήρια τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ ἀκατάκλειστα. — Ἡ γνῶσις κλεῖδα ἔχει, ὡς ὁ Κύριος λέγειτοῖς νομικοῖς· ἄρα πύλη ἐστὶ τοῖς μέν ἀνθρώποις κεκλεισμένη· τὰ γὰρ ἔνδον της πύλης ἐστὶν ὂ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσε, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. — Ὅμοιον δὲ τῆς πύλης ταύτης ἔχει νοῦν καὶ τὸ γεγραμμένον ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ βιβλίον ἐσφραγισμένον· τὸ αὐτὸ τοῦτο βιβλίον λευκοτέρως εὑρήσεις καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἀποκαλύψει Ἰωάννου, καὶ τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα· καὶ πῶς ἤνοιξεν ὁ ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα ταῦτα καὶ μόνος μέχρι γὰρ οὗ ἦλθεν ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς, ἐκέκλειστο ὁ νόμος, ὁ λόγος ὁ προφητικός· καὶ κάλυμμα ἦν ἐπὶ τούτων ὁ λίθος τῆς πωρώσεως, ὂν ἀφεῖλεν ὁ Ἰακὼβ ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος· ἐν πολλοῖς γὰρ τόποις τὸν νοῦν τὸν περὶ τῆς πύλης ταύτης ἡ Γραφὴ ἤνοιξεν.
thought_title: The closed east gate as the hidden mysteries of God
orientation: Origen is commenting on Ezekiel's vision of the closed east gate of the sanctuary, interpreting it as the hidden mysteries of God.
pass_a_gloss: Many gates the son of man Ezekiel describes, and about each he related something; but now he relates to those having ears, about the gate of the holy things, the one looking toward the east; about which it has been written that this gate will be closed, and the things following. — Not only because the Lord the God of Israel passes through the gate, it is closed, but because also the ruler sits in that gate to eat before the Lord along the way of Ailam, which is translated vestibule of the gate. — A gate it is, closed, the mysteries of God, the unclosed things. — Knowledge has a key, as the Lord says to the lawyers; therefore a gate it is, to human beings closed; for the things inside the gate are what eye did not see and ear did not hear, and the things following. — Similar to this gate has a meaning also the scroll sealed, written in Isaiah; this same scroll more clearly you will find also in the Revelation of John, and the things written about it; and how the one from the tribe of Judah opened these things, and alone; for until the Lord our Jesus the Christ came, the law was closed, the prophetic word; and a veil was upon these, the stone of hardness, which Jacob removed from the well; for in many places the mind about this gate the Scripture opened.

choices.why: The genitive plural ἁγίων refers to the sanctuary, the holy place; rendering as 'holy things' keeps the neuter plural sense of the sacred precinct.
The glossary requires 'closed' for κεκλεισμένη, not 'sealed' or 'shut', to keep the distinction from the sealed scroll.
The word is a rare negative adjective from κατακλείω; rendering literally as 'unclosed things' preserves the paradox that the mysteries are both closed and unclosed.
The glossary requires 'sealed scroll' for βιβλίον ἐσφραγισμένον, not 'closed book'.
The glossary requires 'stone of hardness' for λίθος τῆς πωρώσεως, not 'hardened stone' or 'stone of blindness'.

choices.english: the one from the tribe of Judah
choices.why: This is a title for Jesus Christ from Revelation 5:5; rendering literally as 'the one from the tribe of Judah' preserves the biblical allusion.

bible_refs.note: ὁ ἡγούμενος κάθηται ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ πύλῃ τοῦ φαγεῖν ἔναντι Κυρίου
ὃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσε

pass_b_english: Ezekiel, the son of man, describes many gates, and he has something to say about each one. Now he speaks to those who have ears about the gate of the holy things that faces east. It is written of it: “This gate shall be closed,” and so on (Ezekiel 44:1). It is closed not only because the Lord, the God of Israel, passes through the gate, but also because the prince sits in that gate to eat before the Lord by way of Ailam, which means the vestibule of the gate (Ezekiel 44:3).

The closed gate is the mysteries of God, the unclosed things. Knowledge has a key, as the Lord says to the lawyers (Luke 11:52). So the gate is closed to human beings, for what is inside the gate is what no eye has seen and no ear has heard, and so on (1 Corinthians 2:9).

The sealed scroll written about in Isaiah has the same meaning as this gate (Isaiah 29:11). You will find this same scroll more clearly in the Revelation of John, along with what is written about it, and how the one from the tribe of Judah opened these things, and he alone (Revelation 5:5). For until our Lord Jesus Christ came, the law and the prophetic word were closed, and over them lay a veil, the stone of hardness, which Jacob removed from the well. In many places Scripture has opened up the meaning of this gate.
notes: The source text has 'κεκλεισμένι' which appears to be a typographical error for 'κεκλεισμένη' (nominative feminine singular), matching the feminine noun πύλη.
The source text has 'ἐρ μηνεύεται' with a space, likely a typographical error for 'ἑρμηνεύεται' (is translated).
The source text has 'ὂ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς' with a rough breathing on ὂ, likely a typographical error for 'ὃ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς' (what the eye).
The source text has 'λευκοτέρως' which is unusual; it may be a variant or error for 'λαμπρότερον' or 'σαφέστερον' (more clearly), but the literal sense 'more whitely' or 'more clearly' is retained.

last_rejected.why: English identifies the gate as the mysteries, whereas the Greek says the gate is closed and the mysteries of God are unclosed.
last_rejected.fix: The gate is closed, while the mysteries of God remain unclosed.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek 'Πύλη ἐστὶ κεκλεισμένι, τὰ μυστήρια...' equates gate with mysteries; English captures this. No meaning change.
